text:
1. Education begins with stories.
2. Children hear stories before they train their bodies.
3. The founders of the city must supervise the makers of stories.
4. Socrates lays down two laws governing what may be said about the gods.
5. God is good.
6. Because God is good, God is the cause only of good things.
7. The evils in the world far outnumber the goods.
8. Some cause other than God must be found for the evils in the world.
9. Nothing good can cause harm.
10. God does not change.
11. God does not deceive.
12. Whatever is in the best condition is least altered by outside forces.
13. A perfect being would never willingly change for the worse.
14. Homer's story of the two jars at Zeus's threshold must be excluded.
15. Poets who blame a god for the ruin of a household must be excluded.
16. Stories of gods who change their shape must be excluded.
17. The lie that gods and humans hate most is the lie in the soul, not the spoken lie.
18. The lie in the soul is being deceived about reality in the most important part of oneself.
19. A god has no lie in the soul.
20. A god has no motive to put a lie in anyone else's soul.
